cleanRoom.source: Repo-owned Excel/MSForms fixture input generated through public Excel/VBIDE automation and driven with public Windows input.
cleanRoom.prohibited: No Office internals, decompilation, disassembly, non-public source, or OxForms output comparison.

notes: esq.15 settled the held DEFAULT-BUTTON Enter (activates once); oxforms-uvh asks the analogous question for the CANCEL button (held Escape) and an ACCELERATOR button (held Alt+accelerator): does the activation re-fire per OS auto-repeat, or once?

A TextBox1 focus host, a CancelButton whose Cancel property is set True at RUNTIME in UserForm_Initialize (never a design-time fixture property, mirroring the held-key OkButton.Default gotcha), and an AccelButton whose '&Apply' caption makes Alt+A its accelerator (caption is a plain property, safe design-time).

Every Enter/Click/KeyDown/KeyUp handler logs one W008HeldCancelAccelLog row recording the count-relevant arg (KeyCode before/after for keys; none for Click/Enter), the post-handler focus owner (so whether Escape/Alt+A TRANSFERS focus to the button, like Enter->Default did, is observable), and TextBox1.Text. A held key yields one row per OS repeat, so the Click count answers uvh.
No control fonts are declared/applied (a design-time font set hangs the SaveAs dialog). Two scenarios via SetW008Scenario* before each held gesture: held_escape_cancel and held_alt_accelerator.
